{"entries":[{"name":"三四郎","reading":"さんしろう","category":"character","keys":["三四郎","三四郎は"],"content":"The protagonist of the novel, a student from Kumamoto who is travelling by third-class train toward Tokyo. {"entries":[{"name":"里見美禰子","reading":"さとみみねこ","category":"character","keys":["里見美禰子","美禰子","里見","里見さん","団扇を持った女","団扇の女","若いほう","若い女","女","池の女"],"content":"A young woman who is the same person as the figure 三四郎 had called 池の女 and 団扇を持った女, the woman with the fan and white flower on the hill by the pond. When 三四郎 says he came to sweep, she offers to wait with him, and then sits on the veranda. She gives him her name card, which reads 里見美禰子 and gives an address in 本郷真砂町, just across the valley from his lodging. She says they have met before, at the hospital."},{"name":"三四郎","reading":"さんしろう","category":"character","keys":["三四郎","三四郎は"],"content":"The protagonist of the novel, a student from Kumamoto who is travelling by third-class train toward Tokyo. He is still in school, and he wears an old cap with a school insignia. On the train he talks with a bearded man, whom he later learns is 広田, and he feels that man's words have become meaningful since he began attending university lectures. Later he watches two women on a hill by a pond at sunset, and he is fascinated by their colours. He visits 野々宮 and is startled by a woman he calls 池の女 at the end of a long corridor, and he memorises her posture and clothes. He then meets 広田 and 与次郎, and bows to 広田 with his cap in an in-between manner. In the garden he is asked to sweep, and he sits on the veranda until 里見美禰子 enters; she gives him her name card and they recognise each other from the hospital."},{"name":"広田","reading":"ひろた","category":"character","keys":["髭のある男","髭のある人","男","広田","広田さん","広田先生","水蜜桃の先生","青木堂の先生","水蜜桃の男"],"content":"A former high school teacher of 三四郎 and 野々宮, who was previously the unnamed bearded man on the third-class train. He is about forty, with a long, thin face, a thick beard, and a straight nose, and he looks something like a Shinto priest. He shares peaches with 三四郎 on the train and tells him about 子規. He visited 野々宮's sister in hospital, and 三四郎 now sees him drinking tea and smoking alone at 青木堂, wearing a suit. 三四郎 had earlier suspected that this man was the teacher who rode the stubborn horse at the main gate and was laughed at by a craftsman from 喜多床; the passage confirms that the horse incident was indeed Hirota, and 三四郎 concludes that the peach-eating man must be him too, though he admits this is somewhat unreasonable. 与次郎 is with him, and 三四郎 bows to him, neither too formal nor too casual. When 与次郎 introduces him to 三四郎 as the 高等学校 teacher, he says \"知ってる、知ってる\" twice, and 与次郎 looks puzzled but does not ask why he knows 三四郎."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"清","reading":"きよ","category":"character","keys":["清","婆さん"],"content":"Kiyo is a maidservant (下女) who has served the narrator's family for ten years. She comes from a once-dignified family but fell into poverty after the 瓦解 and became a servant. She apologized tearfully to the narrator's father, which eased his anger when he was about to disown the narrator. Despite the narrator's rough reputation, she dotes on him and praises him as 真っ直でよいご気性. She buys him sweets, a sleeping snack, shoes, socks, pencils and notebooks. She retrieved his wallet from the privy and exchanged the ruined 1-yen note for three silver yen, and the narrator never repaid her."},{"name":"おやじ","reading":"おやじ","category":"character","keys":["おやじ"],"content":"The narrator's father, who is unnamed in the text. He was furious with the narrator and nearly disowned him, but his anger was eased by Kiyo's apology. The narrator was not very afraid of him. The father is constantly exasperated with the narrator and finds him hard to handle."},{"name":"おれ","reading":"おれ","category":"character","keys":["おれ"],"content":"The first-person narrator of the book, who is unnamed. As a child he was considered a rough troublemaker by the neighborhood and was shunned. He believed he could not be liked by people, so he was puzzled by Kiyo's affection. He dislikes flattery and resents being treated as someone to be admired."},{"name":"赤シャツ","reading":"あかシャツ","category":"character","keys":["赤シャツ","教頭"],"content":"The vice-principal (教頭), a 文学士 (Bachelor of Arts graduate) whose real name is not given in this passage. He has an oddly gentle, feminine voice and wears red flannel undershirts all year round, even in the summer heat. He claims the red is good for his health, which the narrator finds ridiculous and pretentious. The narrator considers him to look down on people."},{"name":"古賀","reading":"こが","category":"character","keys":["古賀"],"content":"An English teacher at the school, introduced at the very end of this passage. He is noted for having a very pale complexion. The passage breaks off before more is said about him."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"おれ","reading":"おれ","category":"character","keys":["おれ"],"content":"The first-person narrator of the book, who is unnamed. As a child he was considered a rough troublemaker by the neighborhood and was shunned. He believed he could not be liked by people, so he was puzzled by Kiyo's affection. He dislikes flattery and resents being treated as someone to be admired. He gives the staff nicknames, and he dislikes anglers and hunters, believing that people who kill animals for pleasure are unkind. He refuses to be impressed by 赤シャツ's fishing boasts. He reluctantly agreed to the fishing trip, reasoning that refusing would make 赤シャツ suspect he simply could not fish. On the boat he felt irritated by 野だ's remarks and by 赤シャツ's secretive talk about マドンナ, and he later announced he intended to negotiate with 山嵐 about the 堀田 matter."},{"name":"赤シャツ","reading":"あかシャツ","category":"character","keys":["赤シャツ","教頭"],"content":"The vice-principal (教頭), a 文学士 (Bachelor of Arts graduate) whose real name is not given in this passage. He has an oddly gentle, feminine voice and wears red flannel undershirts all year round, even in the summer heat. He claims the red is good for his health, which the narrator finds ridiculous and pretentious. The narrator considers him to look down on people. He invited the narrator to go fishing, boasting that he would teach him, and laughed 'ホホホホ' when the narrator mentioned a carp he once lost. The narrator refused the invitation, disliking anglers and hunters, but later went on the boat trip with 野だ. On the boat he admired the scenery, compared a pine tree to a painting by Turner, and objected to going too close to the island's rocks. He brushed off talk of マドンナ with a strange laugh, and when the narrator said he would confront 山嵐, he grew flustered, warned against violence, and asked whether the narrator meant to cause trouble at the school. He always brings along 野だ (吉川) when he goes out."},{"name":"堀田","reading":"ほりた","category":"character","keys":["堀田","堀田君","山嵐","数学の教師"],"content":"The mathematics teacher, a sturdy man with a close-cropped head who looks like a fierce warrior monk from Mount Hiei. When the narrator politely showed him his appointment letter, he ignored it and casually invited him to visit, laughing 'アハハハ'. The narrator found this rude and gave him the nickname 山嵐. He is a fellow teacher of the narrator, who teaches mathematics. The narrator plans to confront him in a 談判 (negotiation), and 赤シャツ is anxious about this, saying he never clearly committed himself on the matter concerning 堀田."},{"name":"吉川","reading":"よしかわ","category":"character","keys":["吉川","吉川君","野だ","野だいこ","画学の教師"],"content":"The drawing (art) teacher, nicknamed 野だいこ by the narrator. He is theatrical, wearing a flashy silk haori and fluttering a fan, and he claims to be a Edo native (江戸っ子) when told the narrator is from Tokyo, which the narrator finds unconvincing. He is a sycophant who follows 赤シャツ everywhere, visiting his house morning and night and accompanying him wherever he goes, so he appears more like a servant than an equal. Because of this, the narrator suspects he is only a companion to 赤シャツ. On the boat trip he said that sea fishing uses no rod, only line, and he praised the pine tree as Turner-like. He proposed naming the uninhabited island ターナー島, and he suggested painting マドンナ on a rock there."},{"name":"船頭","reading":"せんどう","category":"character","keys":["船頭"],"content":"The unnamed boatman who takes the narrator, 赤シャツ and 野だ out to sea. He rows alone, slowly but skillfully, and the boat is long and narrow in a style the narrator has never seen in Tokyo. He quickly carries them far from the shore."},{"name":"マドンナ","reading":"マドンナ","category":"character","keys":["マドンナ"],"content":"A woman who is discussed but not present in this passage, whose real identity is unclear. 野だ jokingly suggests painting her in a Raphael style on a rock of the island. 赤シャツ objects to talk of her and laughs strangely, and the narrator suspects she may be a nickname for a geisha known to 赤シャツ. The narrator finds the whole matter irrelevant to himself."},{"name":"青嶋","reading":"あおしま","category":"place","keys":["青嶋","ターナー島"],"content":"A small island visible from the sea, described as uninhabited and covered only with stones and pine trees. 野だ proposes renaming it ターナー島 after the painter Turner, and 赤シャツ agrees. The narrator wishes to go ashore on its rocky part, but 赤シャツ objects that the boat cannot go too close to the rocks if they want to fish."},{"name":"高柏寺","reading":"こうはくじ","category":"place","keys":["高柏寺"],"content":"A temple near the shore whose five-storey pagoda rises above the trees and looks sharp like a needle when seen from the sea as the boat departs."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"赤シャツ","reading":"あかシャツ","category":"character","keys":["赤シャツ","教頭"],"content":"The vice-principal (教頭), a 文学士 (Bachelor of Arts graduate) whose real name is not given. He has a gentle, feminine voice and wears red flannel undershirts all year round, claiming the red is good for his health, which the narrator finds ridiculous. He invited the narrator fishing, laughed 'ホホホホ' at the narrator's story of a lost carp, and went on a boat trip with 野だ (吉川), whom he always brings along. On the boat he admired the scenery, compared a pine to a Turner painting, and brushed off talk of マドンナ. He later asked the narrator, sweating, to keep yesterday's matter secret and not speak of it, then asked again whether he was all right. The narrator finds his requests illogical and suspects he doubts the narrator's honesty, and when the narrator mentioned confronting 山嵐 he became flustered and warned against violence."},{"name":"おれ","reading":"おれ","category":"character","keys":["おれ"],"content":"The first-person narrator of the book, who is unnamed. As a child he was considered a rough troublemaker and was shunned, so he doubted anyone could like him, and he dislikes flattery. He gives the staff nicknames and dislikes anglers and hunters, so he reluctantly joined the fishing trip with 赤シャツ and 野だ, where he felt irritated by 野だ's remarks and 赤シャツ's secretive talk about マドンナ. He later said he intended to negotiate with 山嵐 about the 堀田 matter. When 赤シャツ asked him to keep yesterday's matter secret, he agreed, and he regards breaking a promise as shameful. He resents being doubted by 赤シャツ, whom he sees as effeminate and illogical, and he considers himself a man who keeps his word."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"羽柴壮太郎","reading":"はしばそうたろう","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮太郎","壮太郎氏","羽柴氏","おとうさま","主人"],"content":"Business leader (実業界の大立者) and head of the Hashiba family, who lives in a large mansion in Azabu. He is the father of 壮一, 早苗 and 壮二. He had opposed his eldest son's wish to go to the South Seas, and the son ran away from home ten years ago. He keeps the six Romanov diamonds in a safe in his study, and he remains calm when he receives the thief's threatening notice."},{"name":"羽柴壮一","reading":"はしばそういち","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮一","壮一君"],"content":"The eldest son of 羽柴壮太郎. As a teenager he was an adventurous boy who wanted to start a business in the South Seas, but his father refused, so he left home about ten years ago by stowaway on a small sailing ship. He later became a rubber plantation owner near Sandakan on Borneo, and he wrote to his father about three months before the story, asking to come home and apologize. He is about thirty, with a moustache, and is expected to return by plane via Shimonoseki."},{"name":"羽柴早苗","reading":"はしばさなえ","category":"character","keys":["早苗","早苗さん","お嬢さん"],"content":"The daughter of 羽柴壮太郎 and the younger sister of 壮一. The notice shows that he knows exactly where the diamonds are kept, in the study safe."},{"name":"羽柴家の邸宅","reading":"はしばけのていたく","category":"place","keys":["羽柴家","やしき","邸宅","大邸宅"],"content":"A huge mansion in a town in Azabu, covering about 100 meters square and surrounded by a tall concrete wall with an iron gate. {"entries":[{"name":"二十面相","reading":"にじゅうめんそう","category":"character","keys":["二十面相","怪盗","賊","余","二〇","怪青年","盗賊"],"content":"A notorious thief (怪盗) who sends a threatening notice to 羽柴壮太郎 announcing that he will take the six large Romanov diamonds, which he claims to have obtained without payment. He gives no exact date, only warning that the Hashiba family should be very careful. The notice shows that he knows exactly where the diamonds are kept, in the study safe. On the evening of 壮一's return he sends a telegram to the Hashiba household, signed 二〇, saying that he will come at twelve o'clock tonight to collect the promised item. That night he appears in the study disguised as 羽柴壮一, and when 壮太郎 tries to call for help he draws a small pistol and threatens him, calling him 羽柴さん. He mocks the father's confusion and admits he is the thief, not the real son. He explains that he learned of 壮一's disappearance, obtained an earlier photograph of him, and imagined how he would look after ten years, creating the disguise; he claims the photograph shown to the family was of himself. He says he has taken the diamonds, and he speaks with calm confidence while openly boasting of his success."},{"name":"羽柴壮太郎","reading":"はしばそうたろう","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮太郎","壮太郎氏","羽柴氏","おとうさま","主人","羽柴さん","おとうさん"],"content":"Business leader (実業界の大立者) and head of the Hashiba family, who lives in a large mansion in Azabu. He is the father of 壮一, 早苗 and 壮二. He had opposed his eldest son's wish to go to the South Seas, and the son ran away from home ten years ago. He keeps the six Romanov diamonds in a safe in his study, and he remains calm when he receives the thief's threatening notice. He welcomes 壮一 home at Haneda Airport and rides with him in the car. During the family dinner a telegram arrives from 二十面相 reading that the thief will come at midnight to collect the promised item; after reading it he falls silent, then warns the children that they must be very careful that night. In the study that night he is confronted by the man he believes is his son, who is actually 二十面相 in disguise. He is shocked by the mocking manner, and when he moves toward the wall bell he is threatened with a pistol and forced to stand still. He is left unable to explain the letter from Borneo or the photograph, and the thief takes the diamonds."},{"name":"羽柴壮一","reading":"はしばそういち","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮一","壮一君","おにいさま","長男"],"content":"The eldest son of 羽柴壮太郎. As a teenager he was an adventurous boy who wanted to start a business in the South Seas, but his father refused, so he left home about ten years ago by stowaway on a small sailing ship. He later became a rubber plantation owner near Sandakan on Borneo, and he wrote to his father about three months before the story, asking to come home and apologize. He is about thirty, with a moustache, and is expected to return by plane via Shimonoseki. He arrives at Haneda Airport, where the whole family meets him; he is stylishly dressed in a brown overcoat and a double-breasted suit, is tanned, and looks like his photographs but even more handsome. He rides in a car between his parents, and at dinner that evening he tells stories of the South Seas and of his childhood. That night, a man presenting himself as 壮一 appears in the study, but he is revealed to be the thief 二十面相 in disguise, not the real son, and the thief claims the photograph of the son was really of himself."},{"name":"ロマノフ王家の大ダイヤモンド","reading":"ろまのふおうけのだいだいやもんど","category":"item","keys":["ロマノフ王家の大ダイヤモンド","大ダイヤモンド","六個のダイヤモンド","ダイヤモンド","宝石"],"content":"Six large diamonds that were once set in the crown of the Romanov royal family. After the fall of the Russian imperial government, a White Russian took them from the crown and sold them to a Chinese merchant, and they eventually were bought by 羽柴壮太郎. They are valued at two million yen and were kept in a safe in 羽柴壮太郎's study, and they were the target of 二十面相's threat. On the night of 壮一's return, the thief in disguise in the study tells 壮太郎 that he has taken them, so the diamonds have been stolen."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"羽柴壮太郎","reading":"はしばそうたろう","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮太郎","壮太郎氏","羽柴氏","おとうさま","主人","羽柴さん","おとうさん"],"content":"Business leader (実業界の大立者) and head of the Hashiba family, who lives in a large mansion in Azabu. He is the father of 壮一, 早苗 and 壮二. He had opposed his eldest son's wish to go to the South Seas, and the son ran away from home ten years ago. He keeps the six Romanov diamonds in a safe in his study, and he remains calm when he receives the thief's threatening notice. He welcomes 壮一 home at Haneda Airport and rides with him in the car. During the family dinner a telegram arrives from 二十面相 reading that the thief will come at midnight to collect the promised item; after reading it he falls silent, then warns the children that they must be very careful that night. In the study that night he is confronted by the man he believes is his son, who is actually 二十面相 in disguise. He is shocked by the mocking manner, and when he moves toward the wall bell he is threatened with a pistol and forced to stand still. The thief later reveals that the letter from Borneo and the photograph were his own fabrication, leaving 壮太郎 deceived by the whole scheme, and the thief then takes the diamonds."},{"name":"羽柴壮一","reading":"はしばそういち","category":"character","keys":["羽柴壮一","壮一君","おにいさま","長男"],"content":"The eldest son of 羽柴壮太郎. As a teenager he was an adventurous boy who wanted to start a business in the South Seas, but his father refused, so he left home about ten years ago by stowaway on a small sailing ship. He had supposedly become a rubber plantation owner near Sandakan on Borneo, and he wrote to his father about three months before the story, asking to come home and apologize. He is about thirty, with a moustache, and was expected to return by plane via Shimonoseki. A man presenting himself as 壮一 arrived at Haneda Airport, where the whole family met him; he was stylishly dressed in a brown overcoat and a double-breasted suit, tanned, and resembled his photographs but more handsome. That night, the man in the study was revealed to be the thief 二十面相 in disguise, not the real son. The thief then states that the real 壮一 has not been found, is still missing, and is not in Borneo at all, and that the letter and photograph sent from Borneo were staged by 二十面相 through a friend there."},{"name":"二十面相","reading":"にじゅうめんそう","category":"character","keys":["二十面相","怪盗","賊","余","二〇","怪青年","盗賊"],"content":"A notorious thief (怪盗) who sends a threatening notice to 羽柴壮太郎 announcing that he will take the six large Romanov diamonds, which he claims to have obtained without payment. He gives no exact date, only warning that the Hashiba family should be very careful. The notice shows that he knows exactly where the diamonds are kept, in the study safe. On the evening of 壮一's return he sends a telegram to the Hashiba household, signed 二〇, saying that he will come at twelve o'clock tonight to collect the promised item. That night he appears in the study disguised as 羽柴壮一, and when 壮太郎 tries to call for help he draws a small pistol and threatens him, calling him 羽柴さん. He mocks the father's confusion and admits he is the thief, not the real son. He explains that he learned of 壮一's disappearance, obtained an earlier photograph of him, and imagined how he would look after ten years, creating the disguise. He reveals that he wrote the Borneo letter and photograph himself and had a friend in Borneo mail them, that 壮一 never went to Borneo and is still missing, and that the whole affair was his staged play. He calls himself a ninja-like magician and explains that he threw a ping-pong ball onto the carpet to distract the father, who looked under the desk, and in that moment took the diamonds from the jewelry box with ease before leaving with a laugh."},{"name":"ロマノフ王家の大ダイヤモンド","reading":"ろまのふおうけのだいだいやもんど","category":"item","keys":["ロマノフ王家の大ダイヤモンド","大ダイヤモンド","六個のダイヤモンド","ダイヤモンド","宝石"],"content":"Six large diamonds that were once set in the crown of the Romanov royal family. After the fall of the Russian imperial government, a White Russian took them from the crown and sold them to a Chinese merchant, and they eventually were bought by 羽柴壮太郎. They are valued at two million yen and were kept in a safe in 羽柴壮太郎's study, and they were the target of 二十面相's threat. While 壮太郎 was distracted by a ping-pong ball thrown by 二十面相, the thief took them from the jewelry box (宝石箱) in the study, and the diamonds are now stolen."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"先生","reading":"せんせい","category":"character","keys":["先生"],"content":"The narrator's teacher, whom he always calls 先生 and whose real name is withheld in the text. The narrator first met him in Kamakura while he was a young student. The narrator is close to him and sees him as a warm, natural presence in his memory. He is married to 静, and the two appear to be a loving couple who often travel together."},{"name":"静","reading":"しず","category":"character","keys":["静","奥さん","奥様"],"content":"The wife of 先生, named 静 in the text. Her husband calls her by name from the next room, and she answers with an obedient, gentle manner. The couple often attend concerts and plays together and take short trips, including to Hakone and Nikko. The narrator observes that they appear to be a harmonious married pair."},{"name":"Ｋ","reading":"Ｋ","category":"character","keys":["Ｋ"],"content":"A childhood friend of the narrator who is called Ｋ in the text. He was the second son of a Shinshu temple priest from the same region as the narrator, and was adopted into a wealthy doctor's family. He left for Tokyo to study with money from his adoptive family, and later lodged in the same boarding house as the narrator, where they shared a room. Earlier, he had been pressured by his family into an arranged marriage that he did not want, and he avoided going home during summer vacation."},{"name":"鎌倉","reading":"かまくら","category":"place","keys":["鎌倉"],"content":"A seaside town where the narrator went for summer swimming at the invitation of a friend, and where he first met 先生. The narrator was left alone there when his friend Ｋ was called back home by a telegram. It is the setting of the narrator's first acquaintance with 先生."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"Ｋ","reading":"Ｋ","category":"character","keys":["Ｋ"],"content":"A childhood friend of the narrator who is called Ｋ in the text. He was the second son of a Shinshu temple priest from the same region as the narrator, and was adopted into a wealthy doctor's family. He left for Tokyo to study with money from his adoptive family, and later lodged in the same boarding house as the narrator, where they shared a room. Earlier, he had been pressured by his family into an arranged marriage that he did not want, and he avoided going home during summer vacation. In Tokyo he was serious and strong-willed, constantly using the word 精進 (single-minded dedication), which the narrator felt described everything he did. The narrator secretly revered him and was in awe of him, and the two of them, though fearful of Tokyo and its people, boasted in their room of their ambition to become truly great."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"ジョバンニ","reading":"じょばんに","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニ","ジョバンニさん"],"content":"A schoolboy in the afternoon class who is sleepy and has little time or books to read because of his work in the mornings and afternoons. When the teacher asks about the Milky Way, he raises his hand but cannot answer, and he turns red in embarrassment while ザネリ giggles at him. He remembers that he and カムパネルラ once read about the galaxy together, and he feels that カムパネルラ did not answer because he was being kind to him, given how much he has withdrawn from friends."},{"name":"カムパネルラ","reading":"かむぱねるら","category":"character","keys":["カムパネルラ","カムパネルラさん"],"content":"A classmate of ジョバンニ who eagerly raises his hand in class but cannot answer when the teacher calls on him. He is the son of 博士, and he and ジョバンニ once read a magazine and a large book about the galaxy together at his house. ジョバンニ believes カムパネルラ knew the answer but stayed silent out of pity, since ジョバンニ has been less friendly and talkative lately."},{"name":"ザネリ","reading":"ざねり","category":"character","keys":["ザネリ"],"content":"A classmate who sits in the seat in front of ジョバンニ. When ジョバンニ fails to answer the teacher's question, ザネリ looks back and giggles at him."},{"name":"博士","reading":"はかせ","category":"character","keys":["博士","カムパネルラのお父さん"],"content":"The father of カムパネルラ, referred to as a doctor. He has a study with large books, and カムパネルラ fetches a big book from it to look at pictures of the galaxy with ジョバンニ."},{"name":"銀河","reading":"ぎんが","category":"term","keys":["銀河","天の川","銀河帯","乳の流れ"],"content":"The faint white band of light across the night sky, also called the Milky Way (天の川). In class the teacher explains that through a large telescope it appears as many small stars, and that its stars are like grains of sand in a river or fat globules in milk. The teacher says that the Earth and Sun float within this band, so people live inside the Milky Way, which looks whiter where it is deeper and more distant."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"ジョバンニ","reading":"じょばんに","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニ","ジョバンニさん"],"content":"A schoolboy in the afternoon class who is sleepy and has little time or books to read because of his work in the mornings and afternoons. When the teacher asks about the Milky Way, he raises his hand but cannot answer, and he turns red in embarrassment while ザネリ giggles at him. He remembers that he and カムパネルラ once read about the galaxy together, and he feels that カムパネルラ did not answer because he was being kind to him, given how much he has withdrawn from friends. He hurries home to a small house in a back-alley town, where his ill mother is resting in bed and his older sister has left food for him. He buys sugar cubes for his mother's milk and eats tomatoes and bread alone. He hopes his father will return soon, since a newspaper reported good northern fishing this year. Classmates tease him about the sea otter coat his father promised him, but カムパネルラ never joins in and looks sympathetic when others do. ジョバンニ still delivers newspapers each morning, and he fondly remembers visiting カムパネルラ's house after school to play with his alcohol-powered model train."},{"name":"カムパネルラ","reading":"かむぱねるら","category":"character","keys":["カムパネルラ","カムパネルラさん"],"content":"A classmate of ジョバンニ who eagerly raises his hand in class but cannot answer when the teacher calls on him. He is the son of 博士, and he and ジョバンニ once read a magazine and a large book about the galaxy together at his house. ジョバンニ believes カムパネルラ knew the answer but stayed silent out of pity, since ジョバンニ has been less friendly and talkative lately. ジョバンニ's father and カムパネルラ's father were friends since childhood, and ジョバンニ's father once took him to カムパネルラ's house. カムパネルラ has a model train powered by an alcohol lamp, and ジョバンニ often stopped by after school to see it. He never teases ジョバンニ about his father and looks uncomfortable when others do."},{"name":"銀河","reading":"ぎんが","category":"term","keys":["銀河","天の川","銀河帯","乳の流れ","銀河のお祭"],"content":"The faint white band of light across the night sky, also called the Milky Way (天の川). In class the teacher explains that through a large telescope it appears as many small stars, and that its stars are like grains of sand in a river or fat globules in milk. The teacher says that the Earth and Sun float within this band, so people live inside the Milky Way, which looks whiter where it is deeper and more distant. The teacher describes the galaxy as lens-shaped, with the Sun near its middle, and says its stars are suns that shine on their own like ours. The class is told that the lens's size and its stars will be covered in the next science lesson. The teacher also says the day is a galaxy festival, and the students are encouraged to go outside and look at the sky."},{"name":"ジョバンニのお母さん","reading":"じょばんにのおかあさん","category":"character","keys":["お母さん","ジョバンニのお母さん"],"content":"ジョバンニ's mother, who is ill and rests in bed in the front room of their small house. She is grateful for the sugar cubes and asks him to eat first, saying she does not want anything yet. She tells him that his sister came home around three o'clock and left tomato food for him. ジョバンニ asks whether her milk was delivered, and she is unsure. She tells him that his father once promised him a sea otter coat."},{"name":"ジョバンニの姉","reading":"じょばんにのあね","category":"character","keys":["姉さん","ジョバンニの姉"],"content":"ジョバンニ's older sister, who is not named in the text. She came home around three o'clock, tidied up the house, and left a tomato dish for ジョバンニ before going out again. She appears only through what others say about her."},{"name":"ジョバンニのお父さん","reading":"じょばんにのおとうさん","category":"character","keys":["お父さん","ジョバンニのお父さん"],"content":"ジョバンニ's father, who is away and has not returned home. He once brought a huge crab shell and deer antlers to the school, which are still kept in the specimen room. ジョバンニ insists that he is a good man who would never do anything bad, and he believes his father will return soon. ジョバンニ's mother is not sure whether he went out to sea. His father was a childhood friend of カムパネルラ's father, and he once promised ジョバンニ a sea otter coat."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"博士","reading":"はかせ","category":"character","keys":["博士","カムパネルラのお父さん","はかせ"],"content":"The father of カムパネルラ, referred to as a doctor. He has a study with large books, and カムパネルラ fetches a big book from it to look at pictures of the galaxy with ジョバンニ. He has a pale, pointed chin, wears black clothes, and stands very straight. On the night カムパネルラ disappears in the river, he stands at the riverbank watching the water and staring at the watch in his right hand. He declares that there is no hope since カムパネルラ fell 45 minutes earlier, then politely thanks ジョバンニ by name and asks whether his father has returned. He received a cheerful letter from ジョバンニのお父さん two days earlier and expected him to arrive that day, so he guesses the ship was delayed, and he invites ジョバンニ and his classmates to visit his house after school the next day."},{"name":"ジョバンニ","reading":"じょばんに","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニ","ジョバンニさん"],"content":"A schoolboy in the afternoon class who is sleepy and has little time or books to read because of his work in the mornings and afternoons. When the teacher asks about the Milky Way, he raises his hand but cannot answer, and he turns red in embarrassment while ザネリ giggles at him. He remembers that he and カムパネルラ once read about the galaxy together, and he feels カムパネルラ did not answer out of pity, since he has become less friendly lately. He lives in a small house in a back-alley town with his ill mother and older sister, and he still delivers newspapers each morning. On the night of the galaxy festival he goes out with カムパネルラ to see the floating lanterns, and when he hears a child has fallen into the river, he runs to the riverbank, where マルソ tells him カムパネルラ jumped in after ザネリ and has not been found. At the riverbank he tries to tell 博士 that he was walking with カムパネルラ, but his throat tightens and he cannot speak. He then runs back toward town, planning to bring milk to his mother and tell her that his father is coming home."},{"name":"ジョバンニのお母さん","reading":"じょばんにのおかあさん","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニのお母さん","お母さん"],"content":"ジョバンニ's mother, who is ill and rests in bed in the front room of their small house. She is grateful for the sugar cubes and asks him to eat first, and she tells him that his sister came home around three o'clock and left tomato food for him. She is unsure whether her milk was delivered, and she tells him that his father once promised him a sea otter coat. On the night of the galaxy festival she lets him go out to see the lanterns, telling him to play more with カムパネルラ and warning him not to go into the river. ジョバンニ plans to bring her milk and tell her that his father is returning home."},{"name":"ジョバンニのお父さん","reading":"じょばんにのおとうさん","category":"character","keys":["ジョバンニのお父さん","お父さん"],"content":"ジョバンニ's father, who is away at sea and has not yet returned home. He once brought a huge crab shell and deer antlers to the school, which are still kept in the specimen room, and he once promised ジョバンニ a sea otter coat. He was a childhood friend of カムパネルラのお父さん, and ジョバンニ insists he is a good man who would never do anything bad. Two days before the festival he sent 博士 a cheerful letter, and 博士 expected him to arrive around that night, but he had not come home yet and the ship may have been delayed."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"武蔵","reading":"むさし","category":"character","keys":["武蔵","武やん","武やアん"],"content":"A seventeen-year-old fighter lying wounded among the dead after a battle at Sekigahara, where his army has lost. He is from the same village as his friend Matahachi, and both left home without permission to join their former lord's army. He has been hit by several bullets without yet realizing it. He thinks of his elder sister and the village elders, and he is linked to Otsu through his village and his friend."},{"name":"又八","reading":"またはち","category":"character","keys":["又八","又やん","又さん"],"content":"A seventeen-year-old villager from the same village as Musashi, who fought in the battle at Sekigahara. He and Musashi left home together to become soldiers, carrying only spears. Despite his hopes, he was used mostly for menial work such as cutting grass and guarding camp, and he has not won any heads. He is the fiancé of Otsu, and his mother and Otsu both opposed his leaving."},{"name":"お通","reading":"おつう","category":"character","keys":["お通","お通さん","七宝寺のお通"],"content":"A young orphan woman raised at Shippoji temple, cold and lonely in manner like incense ash. She is sixteen and is the fiancée of Matahachi, who is a year older. She tried to stop Matahachi from leaving, along with his mother and Musashi's sister, and she is waiting for him at the temple."},{"name":"金吾中納言秀秋","reading":"きんごちゅうなごんひであき","category":"character","keys":["金吾中納言秀秋","金吾中納言","秀秋"],"content":"A lord whose secret switch of allegiance to the Eastern army turned the battle against the Western side. He attacked the Western allies, including Ishida Mitsunari, Ukita, Shimazu and Konishi, which caused the rout. Matahachi and Musashi blame him as a traitor."},{"name":"石田三成","reading":"いしだみつなり","category":"character","keys":["石田三成","石田"],"content":"A commander on the losing side of the battle at Sekigahara. His army was overrun after Kinago Chunagon Hideaki turned against the Western forces."},{"name":"関ヶ原の戦い","reading":"せきがはらのたたかい","category":"event","keys":["戦い","関ヶ原の戦い","激戦"],"content":"A great battle fought in the Keicho 5 (1600) ninth month, on 14 September, in the Sekigahara area. The army Musashi and Matahachi served lost after a traitor, Kinago Chunagon Hideaki, joined the Eastern army. The battle decided the holder of the realm in only half a day, and a heavy rain fell on the battlefield afterward."},{"name":"関ヶ原","reading":"せきがはら","category":"place","keys":["関ヶ原","この関ヶ原地方"],"content":"The area where a major battle was fought in the Keicho 5 (1600) ninth month. After the fighting, rain washed the battlefield and it was littered with dead soldiers. Musashi lies wounded among the corpses here."},{"name":"七宝寺","reading":"しっぽうじ","category":"place","keys":["七宝寺"],"content":"A temple where Otsu lives and was raised as an orphan. Matahachi and Musashi's families and Otsu wait there for the young men to return from the war."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"沢庵","reading":"たくあん","category":"character","keys":["沢庵","沢庵さん","宗彭沢庵","若い禅坊主"],"content":"Sōhō Takuan, a young Zen monk of about thirty from Tajima Province, who is a wandering monk (雲水) staying at Shippoji temple. He is playful and talkative, often teasing Otsu and making her laugh, and he has a religious manner, as when he speaks of the suffering that people bring on themselves through desire. In spring he washes his tattered robe, jokes about the peach blossoms and the Buddha's birthday, and follows Otsu out to gather flowers, commenting on the peace of the scene. He is sympathetic to Otsu and wishes she could be spared the suffering that others bring on themselves."},{"name":"お通","reading":"おつう","category":"character","keys":["お通","お通さん","七宝寺のお通"],"content":"A young orphan woman raised at Shippoji temple, cold and lonely in manner like incense ash. She is sixteen and is the fiancée of Matahachi, who is a year older. She tried to stop Matahachi from leaving, along with his mother and Musashi's sister, and she is waiting for him at the temple. By the end of the year and into April no word has come from Matahachi or Musashi, and she sadly wonders whether they are dead, asking why men go to war. She is often melancholy but is often made to laugh by the monk Takuan, and she gathers wildflowers by the Aida River near the village."},{"name":"武蔵","reading":"むさし","category":"character","keys":["武蔵","武やん","武やアん"],"content":"A seventeen-year-old fighter lying wounded among the dead after a battle at Sekigahara, where his army has lost. He is from the same village as his friend Matahachi, and both left home without permission to join their former lord's army. He has been hit by several bullets without yet realizing it. He thinks of his elder sister and the village elders, and he is linked to Otsu through his village and his friend. Since the new year no word has come from him or Matahachi, and his family has also heard nothing from him."},{"name":"又八","reading":"またはち","category":"character","keys":["又八","又八さん","又やん"],"content":"A young man from the same village as Musashi, who left home without permission with Musashi to join their former lord's army at Sekigahara. He is the fiancé of Otsu, who is a year younger and waits for him at Shippoji temple. Otsu and his family tried to stop him from leaving. No news has come from him since the battle, and by April people believe he is dead."},{"name":"新免伊賀守","reading":"しんめんいがのかみ","category":"character","keys":["新免伊賀守","伊賀守"],"content":"The lord (領主) of the local area. None of his clan has returned from the war, and after the battle soldiers from the Tokugawa side are said to occupy his small castle. His fate is uncertain, and he is among those whose families are presumed to have died."},{"name":"七宝寺","reading":"しっぽうじ","category":"place","keys":["七宝寺","七宝寺の庫裡"],"content":"A temple where Otsu was raised as an orphan and where she now lives and waits for Matahachi. It has a kitchen (庫裡), a well, tea shrubs and peach trees in its grounds. Takuan, a traveling monk from Tajima, stays here during the spring."},{"name":"英田川","reading":"あいだがわ","category":"place","keys":["英田川","河原"],"content":"A river about four or five chō downstream from the village, with riverbanks full of spring wildflowers. Otsu goes there to gather flowers, and Takuan follows her."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"吾輩","reading":"わがはい","category":"character","keys":["吾輩","猫","吾輩は猫である"],"content":"The first-person narrator, a kitten who has no name yet ('名前はまだ無い'). He was born somewhere dark and damp and cried there, then was carried off by a 書生 and abandoned in a bamboo grove beside a large pond. Hungry and cold, he crept into a nearby house through a gap in a broken bamboo fence, where he was repeatedly thrown out by おさん. He later says he stole something of おさん's called 三馬 and that this was his retaliation, though the passage breaks off before explaining it. He regularly visits the neighbouring cat 三毛 through the same gap in the fence."},{"name":"書生","reading":"しょせい","category":"character","keys":["書生","書生さん"],"content":"A student-type young man who first picks up the narrator kitten and lifts him onto his palm. The narrator later learns that 書生 are considered the most fearsome kind of human, and that they are said to catch cats and boil them to eat. He is unnamed in the passage. He smokes tobacco, which the narrator finds odd and which makes him cough. After carrying the kitten a long way he drops him in the bamboo grove and disappears."},{"name":"おさん","reading":"おさん","category":"character","keys":["おさん"],"content":"A maid in the house the narrator sneaks into. She is described as even rougher than the 書生: she grabs the kitten by the scruff of the neck and throws him outside. She repeatedly throws him out each time he climbs back onto the kitchen floor, and the narrator says he became thoroughly fed up with her. He mentions that he once stole her 三馬, which he presents as the reason for his later retaliation."},{"name":"三毛","reading":"みけ","category":"character","keys":["三毛"],"content":"A cat who lives in the neighbouring house. The narrator visits her through the gap in the bamboo fence that he first used to enter the grounds, and he says this route remains his passage to her even up to the time of narration."}]}

{"entries":[{"name":"苦沙弥","reading":"くしゃみ","category":"character","keys":["苦沙弥","苦沙弥先生","苦沙弥君","主人","主人は","彼","先生"],"content":"The master of the house and a schoolteacher, named Kushami (苦沙弥先生) in this passage. The narrator lives in his home. He rarely meets the narrator and shuts himself in his study (臥竜窟) after school. The family thinks he is a great scholar, and he pretends to be one, but in reality he is lazy: he naps, drools on his books, and has a weak stomach with a sallow, flabby complexion. He eats heavily, takes Takadiastase, and reads only a few pages before falling asleep each night. He talks little and twirls the black hair under his nose. He took in the narrator with the words 'そんなら内へ置いてやれ', and the narrator often sits on his lap while he reads the newspaper. He wakes easily at the children's crying and is nervous (神経胃弱性), and he complains to his visitors about how hard teaching is.
